newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa rally seen not over yet.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa rally seen not over yet.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
LIFFE cocoa futures are poised to correct lower in the short-term but analysts said on Tuesday the current rally which has lifted prices to 12-month high was far from over.
Traders called the market to open 10 stg higher.
"Technically, the market is showing a short-term correction, but I won't recommend selling the market. It could still possibly go a bit higher," said Adrian Haylor, an analyst at Sucden.
"It might best to buy on the dips rather than look for a correction as the up move is not over yet," he added.
Cocoa's rally since late week gained momentum after September broke the key resistance at 1,070 stg.
The advance has left a breakaway gap at 1,046 and 1,059 stg, which remains unfulfilled.
On the downside, Haylor pegged immediate support at 1,100, followed by 1,070.
Resistance is seen at Monday's high of 1,140, followed by the June 1996 reaction high of 1,172.
The 14-day relative strength indicator of 74 percent is well in the overbought zone.
On the fundamental front, traders are keeping a close watch on the current wet spell in Ivory Coast.
Broke GNI said forecasters were debating whether the main crop was early this year or just average.
Wet season deluges have brought a usual spate destruction to shanty towns and damage to roads in outlying areas of the capital, Abidjan.
July 1996 rains had been nearly double the long-term level as erratic weather patterns had recently blurred the cross-over between seasons, said one industry weather watcher.
Ivory Coast went on to produce a bumper 200,000 tonnes 1996/97 mid-crop (May-Sept) in its record 1.2 million tonnes harvest year (Oct-Sept).
